title: rwb-integration outbound-file capability: ACE read path, INT-25 source table, data-lake retirement, JOB-10 and JOB-11 split, operation naming, alert event names, deliverFile manifest and job catalog rows not settled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 29, 31, 32, 33, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T3.1, T4, T5.2, T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5, A1.6 and A2.7; Ownership Map tables (interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog, debt_sale_account, notice, document) and API (four P2 admin rows); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 12, 13 and 15; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5, §R5.7 and §R9
section: §1 Story, §2 Business rationale, §7 Acceptance criteria, §8 Business rules, §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.6 Schedules, §12.7 Tables owned, §15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the unsettled and conflicting points of this story. (1) ACE read path: Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37 and 45 and ADR-010 say only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views, while TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T5.2 and T6.2 say P2 reads them directly; by R-PREC the architecture wins and the TSD wording is superseded, so every ACE fact is one REST call to the rwb-source-data contract with a 2 s timeout. (2) INT-25 source: the legacy AC1 builds the synthetic tape from debt_sale_account, which the Ownership Map gives to S6 rwb-debtsale, so the tape rows arrive in the deliverFile manifest and are never read here. (3) Data lake: the legacy story and the FSD A1.5 still describe the INT-19 reporting extract and the INT-20 decision feed as lake files with JOB-13 and JOB-15, while DP-17 and Architecture v5 slides 2, 8, 37 and 44 remove the lake; the extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through deliverFile and the decision feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision, and the lake statements are retired rather than restated. (4) Job ownership: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-10 to rwb-comms + integration while Architecture v5 slide 16 gives the deliverFile activity and the file windows to rwb-integration alone, and the legacy story assumes one Quartz scheduler for JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13 and JOB-15; the split taken is JOB-11 as the platform outbox relay, JOB-10 as a bank-Airflow window with the file built and sent by rwb-integration, and JOB-13 and JOB-15 removed. (5) Operation naming: Architecture v5 slide 16 names GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, while the TSD P2 v3 appendix and the Ownership Map name GET /admin/outbound-items, POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend, GET /admin/outbox/deliveries and POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend; the TSD and Ownership Map names are used and the slide 16 naming is superseded. (6) Alert names: the legacy story alerts on the events rwb.integration.outbound.held and rwb.integration.outbound.failed, which are not event names under DP-14, so the held-file alert is a rule over the held-item series and the failed-file alert a rule over FileFailed and the EXCEPTION status. (7) Manifest: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 16 fix an activity deliverFile(manifest) and a claim-check manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, but not the full payload, the return element or the internal split with a workflow. (8) Job catalog: no source says whether job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11 after the slide 44 split, so this key writes none and leaves it to the job catalog read. (9) Message wording: the FSD P2 Integration v3 rewrites MSG-P1-001 and outranks the story master, so the FSD wording is used.
evidence: TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 'P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data' and T6.2 'The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only' against Architecture v5 slide 9 'only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views' and slide 37 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 rows INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI' and INT-20 'COLLINS, through the data lake' against Architecture v5 slide 2 'Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed'; Architecture v5 slide 44 row JOB-10 'rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers' against slide 16 'TMP Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile · Airflow window: WIN file 16:00, buyer files per lot'; Architecture v5 slide 16 'REST GET /interface-runs (operations) · POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry' against TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 API-P2-001 to API-P2-004 and the Ownership Map rows; Ownership Map debt_sale_account 'S6 owns lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer' against legacy RWB-E1-007 AC1 'builds the synthetic tape of 120 accounts from debt_sale_account and v_ace_account'; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 15 'the Log Analytics alert rule on events rwb.integration.outbound.held and rwb.integration.outbound.failed' against Architecture v5 slide 16 'EVT rwb.integration.events.v1: FileDelivered, FileFailed'.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: ACE read path, source-table ownership, job split, API naming and alerts
proposed: Build the outbound-file capability in rwb-integration on the service base /api/recovery/integration/v1, with interface_config and outbound_item as its own tables and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects as library objects in rwb_integration (DP-01, DP-02, DP-09, DP-15). Read every ACE fact through the rwb-source-data contract one hop and 2 s, and record that the TSD P2 v3 direct-view wording is superseded by Architecture v5 and ADR-010. Take the INT-25 tape rows from the deliverFile manifest that rwb-debtsale sends. Retire the lake statements of INT-19, INT-20, JOB-13 and JOB-15: the extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through deliverFile and the decision feed is Kafka ingest in rwb-decision. Keep JOB-11 as the platform relay and JOB-10 as a bank-Airflow window with the file built and sent here, and register no Schedule for either window. Use the four TSD and Ownership Map admin paths and record slide 16's /interface-runs naming as superseded. Restate the two alerts as rules over the held-item series and over FileFailed, owned by the operations story. Fix the manifest and the return element in the contract story and re-confirm them with rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting. Load the four interface rows as reference data; leave the job_catalog rows to the job catalog read. Confirm with the ACE team that rwb_integration needs no grant on the recovery schema.

title: Outbound-file contract: deliverFile manifest and return, notice-fact read of rwb-comms, JSON field names and problem body, event schema subject and compatibility level not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 17 and 41; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map tables (notice, interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog) and API (four P2 admin rows); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 11, 12 and 13; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG sections 12.2 and 12.5; Template and Rules v1 §R9
section: §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.3 Events published, §12.5 Workflows and activities, §13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the shape-level points that no source fixes for this contract. (1) The manifest of deliverFile: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 16 fix a claim-check manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count and an activity named deliverFile(manifest), but not the interface ID, the business date, the case IDs, the idempotency key, the claim-check link or the requesting service. (2) The return element of deliverFile and the internal split between the activity and a local workflow. (3) The notice-fact read behind INT-14: the legacy story read the notice table in process, notice belongs to P6, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 no notice-fact read, so the operation exists in this contract with no path, query or field name in any source. (4) The JSON field names of the four admin responses and the detail texts of the problem body. (5) The schema-registry subject of rwb.integration.events.v1 and its compatibility level. (6) Whether job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11. (7) The naming difference between Architecture v5 slide 16 (/interface-runs) and the TSD appendix and Ownership Map (/admin/outbound-items and /admin/outbox/deliveries), recorded as a conflict in CG-B-P2-01-E1007-1 and applied here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Manifest: fileId, batchId, sha256, record count' and slide 16 'TMP Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile'; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 'REST POST /notices (request) · GET /cases/{id}/notices' and no notice read by ID; TSD P2 v3 T-A.2 gives the four operations with their query parameters and error codes but no body shape; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives the columns of interface_config, outbound_item, processed_event, idempotency_key, outbox_event, outbox_delivery and job_catalog; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 11 reads notice.sent_date (DF-LEG-019) and notice.person_key (DF-LEG-030) from the notice table in process; the sibling integration story states that the manifest and the claim-check handoff are 'Not specified in the source documents'.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: contract shapes, consumed notice read and event registry
proposed: Fix the manifest, the return element and the three typed failures in RWB-P2-E1007-CON and re-confirm them with rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting. Fix the notice-fact read in the rwb-comms contract with the notice ID, the sent date, the person key and the document ID. Publish one RFC 9457 problem-details body for the four admin operations with the six status codes of the TSD appendix. Fix the JSON names of the four responses in the OpenAPI document. Fix the registry subject and the compatibility level with the platform event owner. Leave the job_catalog rows to the job catalog read. Take the TSD and Ownership Map admin paths and record slide 16's naming as superseded.

title: Outbound egress infrastructure: endpoint names, accounts, folders, receiver ranges, PGP key identifiers, staging names, file-size limit, transfer timeout and rotation period not specified in any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 16, 32 and 35; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052 and NFR-053; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.1; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3; RWB-PLT-N012-INF
section: §3 Preconditions, §6 INVEST check, §8 Business rules, §10 Authority, §11 Data, §13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the infrastructure values of this key. Architecture v5 slides 8, 11, 16 and 32 name the two outbound interfaces (INT-14 WIN registered mail and INT-25 debt buyers), the MFT/SFTP transport with PGP for a party outside the bank and a claim-check link for one file for 15 minutes, and slides 11 and 35 require private access, workload identity and keys in the key store; no source names the endpoint hosts, ports, accounts, folders, file patterns per environment, the receiver ranges, the PGP key identifiers or fingerprints, the staging location names, the maximum file size, the transfer timeout, the connection and read timeouts, the concurrent transfer limit or the rotation period. The 15 minutes of Architecture v5 slide 11 is the validity of the claim-check link and not a transfer budget, so it cannot be used as the timeout.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Transport: Blob + MFT/SFTP; PGP for outside parties' and 'Identity: SAS link, one file, 15 minutes' with no size or timeout value; Architecture v5 slide 35 lists zero trust and private access without naming a range; NFR-052 'Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts' without a rotation period; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3 'The SFTP outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052)' and no folder name.
area: Integration (P2) outbound egress: MFT/SFTP endpoints, keys, network and budgets
proposed: Provision the two endpoints per environment with one receiver and one key each, hold the credentials, private keys and certificates in the key store behind the rwb-integration workload identity, apply the private DNS records and the egress allow-list, stage the file with its manifest and its sha256, and set the size, timeout and concurrency budgets as environment values. Fix every value with the bank MFT team, the network team and security, and record the rotation period in the key-rotation runbook.

title: Outbound-file deployment: chart values, replica counts, KEDA threshold, lag and alert thresholds, dashboard names, build ID format, Airflow trigger contract of the two file windows and the message identifiers of the lag and window alerts not specified in any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 9, 16, 31, 32, 33, 41, 44 and 45; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11; ADR-023; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 and T-A.1; RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG section 12.6; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s14 and §R9
section: §11 Data, §12.6 Schedules, §14 Validation and messages, §13 Solution plan (alert mapping and artefacts)
description: One combined row for the deployment values and identifiers of this key. Architecture v5 slides 9, 33 and 41 fix the topic settings, the KEDA scaling shape and one login per service, and slides 16, 31, 32 and 44 fix the 16:00 WIN window and the per-lot buyer window as bank-Airflow work with rwb-integration building and sending the files, but no source fixes the chart values, the replica counts, the resource sizes, the KEDA backlog threshold, the consumer quotas, the lag and alert thresholds, the dashboard names, the build ID format or the trigger contract of the two windows (the call, its parameters and its idempotency key). The lag alert and the window and endpoint alert also have no message identifier and no agreed text in the source set, so both carry the §R9 placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names them.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-10 WIN notices 16:00 rwb-comms + integration Airflow file window + workers' and slide 32 'rwb-integration still builds the files and manifests; Airflow owns the window, the transfer and the retry' with no call contract; Architecture v5 slide 9 'Kafka: topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, outbox and inbox, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt' with no lag threshold; Temporal and Drools design slide 11 names worker versioning and a build ID without a format; the legacy RWB-E1-007 section 14 lists MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-005, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P2-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and no lag or window alert identifier.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: deployment values, Airflow windows and alert identifiers
proposed: Set the chart values, the replica counts, the KEDA backlog threshold, the lag and alert thresholds and the build ID format as environment values of the operations story. Confirm the two windows with the bank Airflow owner as calls to the requesting services on their own APIs, and record that the deployment registers no Schedule and no timer for either. Fix the trigger contract of the two windows and the message identifiers of the lag and window alerts with the Airflow owner and the platform observability owner, and keep the §R9 placeholder until they are named.
